Commit: 82e7d216b51f2867647bfccaaf532d732fd9e2ec Channel: beta
feat(workshop): filter browsing by age rating
The Workshop browser had no rating filter because the rating never made it past the parser. `toWorkshopItem` stripped `Everyone`, `Questionable` and `Mature` from the tag list alongside the bookkeeping tags like `Approved` and `Wallpaper`, and `WorkshopItem` had no field to hold one, so the grid could not filter on something it never saw. The local library has filtered on `project.json`'s `contentrating` all along, so the two halves of the app disagreed about whether rating was a thing you could filter on.
So read the rating off the raw tags before they are stripped, and carry it on `WorkshopItem` as a `WorkshopAgeRating` whose raw values match `contentrating` - a Workshop item and an installed wallpaper now name the same rating the same way.
Narrowing has to happen server-side: at ~3.1M published files and 30 per page, filtering the page after it arrives would leave the pager reporting counts it cannot deliver. The three ratings are mutually exclusive, so listing several in `requiredtags` ANDs to zero rows, and `match_all_tags` is a query-wide switch that would turn the type and genre filters into ORs too. `excludedtags` is the one mechanism that composes: it is orthogonal to `requiredtags`, so the unchecked ratings drop out while type and genre keep their AND semantics. Verified against the live API - `Scene`+`Anime` with the other two ratings excluded returns 30/30 `Everyone` `Scene` rows.
Two edges are deliberate. A cleared filter stops narrowing instead of excluding all three, which would ask Steam for an empty set and read as a broken browser; the sidebar says so. And a handful of published files carry no rating tag at all, which `excludedtags` cannot exclude - those pass through, matching how the local library treats a missing `contentrating`.
The filter defaults to all-ages and persists, so adult content stays opt-in. Discover's shelves take the same filter as the grid, or a wallpaper filtered out of one would resurface in the other. Cards badge only the restricted ratings, since badging every all-ages wallpaper would mark almost the whole grid.

Commit: de266a7ead06539809dba42fd78c396b1f46be34 Channel: beta
fix(scene): read puppet bone curves as opacity, not pose blend weights
Eyelids stopped covering the pupil for the few frames of a blink. The MDLA block's `blend_curves` were being multiplied into the pose blend weight, so a curve dipping to 0 zeroed that bone's animation delta and snapped it back to its bind pose mid-blink - lid and lash jumped out from over the iris, which then showed through.
They are not blend weights. WE's image shaders declare `uniform float g_BonesAlpha[BONECOUNT]` under SKINNING_ALPHA and multiply the LBS-weighted sample into the vertex alpha; the curve is a per-bone opacity envelope on the timeline. Two facts in the corpus settle it. In 3396722575's eye puppets, five of the bones whose curve drops to 0 hold their TRS completely still through the dip, so under a pose-blend reading the curve is a mathematical no-op and could not do anything at all. And 2910422008's single-bone rigid sprites ramp 0 -> 1 while travelling 300 units, where a pose-blend reading pins the sprite at its bind pose for the whole animation instead of fading it in.
So route the curves to a per-bone alpha computed alongside the pose in genFrame, upload it as g_BonesAlpha, and leave pose blending to the layer's own blend amount. The alpha is deliberately flat per bone with no parent inheritance, matching the shader's g_BonesAlpha[a_BlendIndices.*] lookup - the bones that matter here have no authored motion to inherit. Layer blend scales the envelope toward opaque rather than toward zero, so a layer dialled out contributes no fade instead of darkening the sprite.
SKINNING_ALPHA is set only when a puppet ships a curve that actually leaves 1.0. Of the 38 installed scene wallpapers carrying puppets, four do; the other 34 keep their existing shader permutation and upload path untouched.
std140 gives each element of a scalar array its own 16-byte register, so the upload packs one alpha into .x per register. Writing them contiguously instead leaves every bone past the first quarter reading padding, which renders as fully transparent - during development that erased everything but the pupil.

Commit: 0b0676d103bfd507ed8e4420c4ab4deae54e4fc4 Channel: beta
feat(settings): add the override-wallpaper toggle to the appearance section
Exposes the desktop override as "覆盖壁纸" under 通用 › 外观, which until now had no user-facing control at all — its predecessor was gated on adjustMenuBarTint, a setting no view bound. Off is the default and keeps the previous behaviour of overriding only while Mirage runs, for menu bar and Dock tint consistency; on keeps the override after quitting, the way Wallpaper Engine's option of the same name does.
Both strings are translated in all three tables rather than left equal to their Simplified Chinese keys, which would have read as Simplified in the English and Traditional locales without failing visibly (see 8cfc493).
